subject: Dynamic floor transition — redline and packaging clarifications
messages:
From: Liam Harper <liam.harper@acmehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ng <sam.ng@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on 'dynamic floor' in pricing exhibit

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the pricing exhibit and had a few follow-ups before we push to procurement:

- The "dynamic floor" idea in Exhibit D looks promising, but we need clarity on how the floor updates across seasonal quarters — specifically whether the floor is recalculated monthly or quarter-to-quarter.
- Acme ops would like to understand whether onboarding credits are amortized against the floor (we prefer amortization over 12 months).
- Any clawback/earnout mechanics tied to post-launch usage would need a concrete waterfall example.

I've attached our SOW and a short spreadsheet showing our expected ramp for Q3/Q4. Can Jordan/legal and your billing team confirm whether the proposed language will work from a contract and invoicing perspective?

Thanks,
Liam

Attachments: ACME_SOW_v1.pdf, ACME_ramp_Q3Q4.xlsx

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Liam Harper <liam.harper@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Samantha Ng <sam.ng@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on 'dynamic floor' in pricing exhibit

Hi Liam / Samantha —

Appreciate the ramp details. Quick summary and next steps from our side:

1) Mechanics we propose (see attached Pricing_Exhibit_DynamicFloor.pdf and redlined OrderForm_ACME_RevB_redline.docx):
   - Transitional approach: a 10% transitional floor for the first quarter post-go-live, moving to the agreed standard floor at the start of Q4.
   - Floor recalculation cadence: quarter-to-quarter (recalculated at quarter boundary using prior 3-month realized usage).
   - Onboarding credit treatment: onboarding credit amortized over 12 months and applied as an upfront invoice credit line item (will show on each invoice pro rata).

2) Clawback / earnout example: attached exhibit includes a sample waterfall with explicit bands and timing — Jordan, I've left two open points where legal may want stronger guardrails (ambiguity on "seasonal smoothing" and the trigger that moves from transition floor to standard floor).

3) Ops & billing: Marissa / Ben — can you confirm the invoicing flow below? If OK, we'll incorporate into the MOPs appendix.

Proposed next steps:
- Jordan: legal redline review and concrete edits on earnout language (we'll send the doc back to Acme).
- Marissa / Ben: confirm billing cadence and true-up process.
- Liam / Samantha: quick call tomorrow to walk the waterfall table?

If that schedule works, I'll circulate an updated order form and route for signature (DocuSign) by end of week.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments (from Redwood): OrderForm_ACME_RevB_redline.docx, Pricing_Exhibit_DynamicFloor.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Liam Harper <liam.harper@acmehealth.com>, Samantha Ng <sam.ng@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on 'dynamic floor' in pricing exhibit

Olga / team —

Thanks for the clear summary. I reviewed the redline and left targeted edits; high level comments here so we can converge before sending back to Acme: 

- Remove the undefined term "seasonal smoothing" and replace with explicit metrics-based language ("seasonal adjustment" -> define using 3-month trailing average and explicit caps on adjustment per quarter).
- Cap the magnitude of floor reductions during transitional period to X% (example in attached legal_comments_orderform.pdf includes a 20% downside cap to prevent excessive volatility).
- Add an earnout reconciliation timeline: 60-day true-up after quarter close with netting against onboarding credit amortization. This prevents double-crediting and clarifies invoicing.
- Clarify remedy for disputed usage calculations: require both parties to escalate within 30 days to the designated billing contacts and permit independent audit if unresolved.

Two contract-level asks for Acme to consider: define the orchestration trigger to end the transition (we recommend "90-day sustained utilization above 85% of target band") and confirm that onboarding credit amortization does not reduce reported usage for pricing-floor calculations (i.e., credits are financial only).

I'll attach the PDF with inline comments. Once Marissa confirms the cadence and Ben confirms revenue recognition framing, we can publish the consolidated redline.

Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Commercial | Redwood Inference

Attachment (from Legal): legal_comments_orderform.pdf

Quick operational notes —

- Billing cadence OK with 60-day true-up per Jordan's suggestion, but we need to record the onboarding credit as an invoice-level amortized credit (not as a negative usage metric). That matches our billing system constraints.
- We should restrict the quarterly floor recalculation to only adjust upward more than downward (one-way smoothing) for the first two quarters to avoid churn to Acme's accounting.
- I've attached a mutual-action-plan workbook (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with proposed owners for billing/verifications and a suggested call cadence.

Can we schedule 30 minutes Thursday to walk the MAP and the waterfall table?

Thanks,
Marissa

Liam / Samantha —

Thanks for the thoughtful questions and for sharing the ramp. We've consolidated feedback from legal and ops and attached the revised order form + pricing exhibit redlines for your review: OrderForm_ACME_RevB_redline.docx and Pricing_Exhibit_DynamicFloor.pdf. High-level changes included in the redline: 

- Defined "seasonal adjustment" with 3-month trailing average and a cap on quarterly adjustments (see Section 2.1.3).
- Transitional floor limited to 10% for Q1 post-launch with a one-way smoothing cap for the first two quarters (ops requested).
- Onboarding credit: amortized 12 months, shown as an invoice-level credit; explicitly excluded from usage calculations for floor determination (financial-only treatment).
- Earnout/true-up: 60-day reconciliation window after quarter close with dispute escalation path and audit right.

Action items:
- Please review the attached redline and confirm by EOD Monday whether Acme can accept the guardrails.
- If accepted, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet and route for signature. DocuSign preview link: https://www.docusign.com/packaging/ACME-2025
- If you prefer, we can do a 30-min call Thursday 08:00-08:30 PT to walk the waterfall and MAP.

Thanks again — we're eager to get you live and aligned on a predictable ramp.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
